overview: White supports e4 with f3 and plans Be3, Qd2 and long castling with a kingside pawn storm (g4, h4). Black castles and strikes with ...e5 (locking the centre after d5, then ...f5) or ...c5 and ...Nc6 (Panno/Sämisch Gambit lines). The usual game is opposite-side castling where both sides attack, so timing matters.

white_ideas.idea: Be3, Qd2, O-O-O and a g4/h4 pawn storm.
Gain space with d5 and shut Black's bishop on g7.

black_ideas.idea: ...e5 and ...Nh5/...f5 for kingside play, or ...c5 to hit the centre.
Break with ...b5 or ...a6 and queenside play while White attacks.

typical_structures.structure: Closed centre with White c4/d5/e4/f3 against Black e5/d6 chain.

character.notes: Opposite-side castling races and pawn storms, forced timing.

gambit.notes: No gambit in main lines; the Sämisch Gambit ...c5 is a sub-line.

structure.notes: After d5 and ...e5 the centre locks.

level.notes: Like the KID, Black needs to understand the timing of breaks; theory is long too.

sublines_that_differ.name: Panno
sublines_that_differ.how: Black attacks the centre quickly with ...a6 and ...Rb8.

sublines_that_differ.name: Sämisch Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a pawn for activity.

character.reason: Opposite-side castling races where one slow move can lose.

gambit.reason: No material is given in the main lines.

structure.reason: The centre locks after d5 and ...e5.

level.reason: Like the KID, plans and timing are hard to get right.

plans.reason: White castles long and storms the kingside.
